title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the first draft of 'Analysis situs' (1986), Grothendieck sets up an axiomatic, purely combinatorial framework. A 'contrée' M is a set of 'multiplicités' (roughly strata or cells). It carries two order-like relations, ≤ and ≪, a compatibility/admissibility relation, and a class of 'figures': subsets of M closed downward for ≤ (axiom Fig 2). Each X has an elementary figure F_X. The axioms are called Cont 1–5 and Fig 1–4. The previous page shows that a sub-contrée M' (a ≪-closed subset with the induced structure) again satisfies Cont 1–4 and Fig 1–4.

(1) Completion of that proposition. Cont 5 is also stable under passage to a sub-contrée. Probably also: if M is 'finitiste', so is M'.

(2) Disjointness. Two figures are disjoint if they are compatible and their intersection is empty. Two multiplicities X, Y are disjoint if F_X and F_Y are, i.e. X and Y are compatible and there is no Z in M with Z ≤ X and Z ≤ Y. The margin criterion: F and G are disjoint iff every X in F is disjoint from every Y in G. This follows because figures are ≤-down-closed, so a common element of F and G lies under some X in F and some Y in G.

(3) Refinement. F is 'plus fine' than G (written with a ≪-type symbol) iff for every X in F there is Y in G with X ≪ Y. For elementary figures F_X, F_Y this reduces to X ≪ Y.

(4) Proposition. F is a sub-figure of G iff F is finer than G and compatible with G. Here compatibility of figures is defined through compatibility of multiplicities. Key step: if X ≪ Y and X is compatible with Y, then X ≤ Y, hence X lies in G by Fig 2. The converse is trivial.

Role: this sets up the basic lattice/poset calculus of 'figures', the closed unions of strata. The next page adds Cond 5 (disjointness is inherited by ≪-smaller multiplicities) and deduces that disjointness survives refinement. The whole serves the program of a combinatorial 'tame topology' (topologie modérée) of stratified spaces announced in the Esquisse.
errors: The written proof is labelled 'pour prouver ⇒', but the argument given (X≪Y and compatible ⇒ X≤Y ⇒ X∈G) actually proves the sufficiency 'finer + compatible ⇒ sub-figure'. This is only a labelling issue; the other direction is immediate.

Making disjointness require compatibility (rather than just empty intersection) is a deliberate non-standard choice. Incompatible pairs are therefore neither 'meeting' nor 'disjoint'. This is consistent with Cond 5 / Cond 6 on the next page, but the text oscillates (an 'in' is inserted before 'compatibles' in the main text, while the margin says 'compatibles').

The key implication 'X ≪ Y and X compatible with Y ⇒ X ≤ Y' is invoked without saying which axiom (Cont 1–4) supplies it. Presumably it is one of the Cont axioms of p. 33ff, but this cannot be verified from this page.

ideas.what: Stability of axiom Cont 5 (and finitism) under passage to sub-contrées
ideas.modern_name: hereditary property of a (sub)structure; closed sub-poset of a stratification poset

ideas.what: Disjointness of figures/multiplicities defined via compatibility plus absence of a common ≤-lower bound; pointwise criterion for figures
ideas.modern_name: disjointness of down-sets in a poset of strata (no common lower bound)

ideas.what: Refinement order on figures: F finer than G iff each X∈F is ≪ some Y∈G
ideas.modern_name: refinement preorder (as for covers / Hoare-type powerdomain order on down-sets)

ideas.what: Characterization: sub-figure ⇔ finer and compatible, using 'X≪Y & compatible ⇒ X≤Y'
ideas.modern_name: comparison of two specialization-type orders on strata of a stratified space

missed.claim: The page belongs to an unpublished axiomatic theory of 'contrées' and 'figures': a combinatorial foundation for tame/stratified topology with two orders ≤, ≪ and a compatibility relation. Grothendieck only announced this program (Esquisse, 'topologie modérée') and never published it. This page itself contains only routine definitions.
missed.quote: Pour que F soit une sous-figure de G, il faut et il suffit que F soit plus fine que G, et soit compatible à G
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The axiom system (Cont 1–5, Fig 1–4, Cond 5–6) could be compared with o-minimal cell decompositions, stratified spaces/exit-path posets and combinatorial models of tame topology. Little of this framework is in the literature as Grothendieck's.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine order-theoretic definitions (disjointness, refinement, sub-figure criterion) inside an unpublished axiomatics of tame topology; the framework is of historical interest, but this page contains nothing non-trivial on its own.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 likely reads 'Enfin, si M est finitiste, M' aussi' (or similar), not 'si C est fini[?], C ...'.

In the refinement definition the relation is X ≪ Y (double-angle symbol, possibly underlined), consistent with 'cela signifie donc simplement que X ≪ Y'; the transcription's 'X ≤ Y' there is likely wrong. The notation for 'F plus fine que G' uses a ≪-type symbol rather than ⩽.
The heading was corrected to something like 'Multiplicités et figures disjointes'.

Main text: 'On dit que deux figures sont disjointes si elles sont compatibles, et si leur intersection est vide'; the following line defines X, Y disjoint if F_X, F_Y are, i.e. there is no Z∈M with Z ≤ X, Y.
Margin: 'Pour que F, G soient disj. il faut et il suffit que ∀X∈F, Y∈G, X et Y soient disj.'
